requirement.from: A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. It must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, and the tenant must get a receipt within 30 days naming the bank, location, amount and account number. The tenant must get a signed receipt when the deposit is received, and a written statement of the premises' condition within 10 days after tenancy commences or on receipt of the deposit, whichever is later. If the lessor holds the deposit for a year or longer, it must pay interest at 5% per year (or the lesser amount actually received from the bank) at the end of each year of the tenancy. The lessor must return the deposit, less permitted deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Permitted deductions are unpaid rent or water charges, unpaid tax increases under a conforming escalation clause, and reasonable repair of damage beyond normal wear and tear. Damage deductions require a sworn itemized list with cost evidence within the same 30 days. The lessor must keep deposit records for 2 years after the tenancy ends. The deposit and accrued interest must be transferred to a successor in interest. As amended effective Aug 1, 2025, the Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities may by regulation authorize an optional fee in lieu of a security deposit, capped at 1 month's rent in total with any deposit.

title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
requirement: Residential rental property owners may not pay for or subscribe to a coordinator's services, and no person may perform a coordinating function or engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination using algorithms that rely on competitors' competitively sensitive information to set or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy levels. Violations are unlawful under the New Jersey Antitrust Act, and the Attorney General must establish a complaint location and may adopt rules.
key_value: Ban on use of algorithmic revenue management software or algorithmic devices performing a coordinating function (shared nonpublic data / parallel pricing coordination) for residential rents; effective July 1, 2027
coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential dwelling units in New Jersey (houses, apartments, accessory units or other units intended as a primary residence) and to any rental property owner, coordinator or other person. Municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances, except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by any other law.
exemptions: Residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. The following are excluded from 'coordinating function': research, statistical analysis or testing not used to set or recommend terms; free public rent estimates; real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set or recommend prices or collect sensitive information to do so; and government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls. Government entities are not 'coordinators', and parallel pricing required by affordability controls is not covered. Algorithmic devices exclude spreadsheets that do not use AI and require human analysis.

title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (Just Cause for Termination of Tenancy)
requirement: A landlord may not terminate a covered residential tenancy without at-fault just cause (such as non-payment, material lease breach, nuisance or criminal activity) or good-faith no-fault just cause (owner or family move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court vacate order, or demolition or substantial remodel), and the termination notice must state the cause. No-fault terminations require 30 or 60 days' notice under Civ. Code § 1946.1, relocation assistance, notice to the San Diego Housing Commission, and in specified cases a right of first offer to re-rent within five years; buyout agreements are regulated and retaliation is prohibited.
